overview: This Senate resolution marks three years since the November 19-20, 2022, mass shooting at Club Q, an LGBTQ+ bar in Colorado Springs, Colorado. It names the five people killed, notes that dozens more were injured, and praises the patrons who disarmed the shooter. It also mentions community efforts to build a memorial and a resource center for survivors. The resolution expresses the Senate's continued solidarity with the survivors, the local LGBTQ+ community and the victims' families. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say it honors the victims and those who stopped the attack, and affirms that violence targeting people for who they are is unacceptable.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
